# Physics

@difference Extension: the original has no rigid body physics. `CreatePhysicsBody` and the commands that start with `Physics` add bodies that fall, collide, slide and rest, simulated by Jolt. Nothing in a program that does not use them changes.

A physics body is an entity, so it can be moved, hidden and freed like any other, but it is not a collider: a body is never part of `Collisions`, `EntityType` on it is an error, and the picks of `LinePick` and `EntityPick` do not see it. The two worlds are separate on purpose, so a program pays for physics only when it creates a body.

## Bodies

[CreatePhysicsBody](CreatePhysicsBody) makes a body in the shape of a box, sphere, ellipsoid, capsule, cylinder or tapered capsule. [CreatePhysicsBodyFromEntity](CreatePhysicsBodyFromEntity) makes a new body from the vertices of an entity (a box, a convex hull or, for static bodies, the mesh), and leaves that entity as it was. Parent the visible mesh to the body with `EntityParent mesh, body, True` to make it follow.

A body is static (does not move), kinematic (moved by the program, pushes others) or dynamic (moved by the simulation). [PhysicsBodyMotion](PhysicsBodyMotion) changes it. A mesh can be static or kinematic, never dynamic.

## Stepping

[PhysicsUpdate](PhysicsUpdate) moves time forward by the seconds that are given (or by the time since its last call). `UpdateWorld` does not step physics. [PhysicsMode](PhysicsMode) 0 (default) simulates in steps of 1 / [PhysicsRate](PhysicsRate) seconds, at most [PhysicsMaxSteps](PhysicsMaxSteps) per call, and `RenderWorld` draws bodies between the last two steps, so motion is smooth at any frame rate. Mode 1 does one step with the time that is given, without smoothing.

Moving a body entity with `PositionEntity` or `RotateEntity` teleports the body to the new pose at the next `PhysicsUpdate`.

## Solver

[PhysicsSolver](PhysicsSolver) picks a preset: 0 balanced, 1 fast, 2 accurate (continuous collision on) and 3 custom, which any single setting such as [PhysicsVelocityIterations](PhysicsVelocityIterations) selects. The simulation is deterministic for the same inputs on every thread count.

## Worlds

[CreatePhysicsWorld](CreatePhysicsWorld) makes another world that has its own gravity, settings and bodies, and every command that takes a world has a trailing `world` argument, where 0 is the default world.

Turning commands such as [PhysicsApplyTorque](PhysicsApplyTorque) use degrees and the turning sense of `TurnEntity`; vectors are in the space of the body unless `global` is true.

## Queries and contacts

[PhysicsRayCast](PhysicsRayCast) finds the closest body on a line, [PhysicsPointInside](PhysicsPointInside) the body that holds a point, and [PhysicsOverlapSphere](PhysicsOverlapSphere) and [PhysicsOverlapBox](PhysicsOverlapBox) the bodies that touch a sphere or a box. They look only at the bodies of one physics world (the default one or the one given by the trailing `world` argument), never at colliders or at what `LinePick` sees, and only at the layers named by their masks. Sensors are left out unless the query asks for them, which is how a region that notices what is inside of it is made.

[PhysicsContactReport](PhysicsContactReport) makes a body report what touches it. After each [PhysicsUpdate](PhysicsUpdate), [GetPhysicsContactCount](GetPhysicsContactCount) tells how many pairs touched and the `GetPhysicsContact` commands, such as [GetPhysicsContactEntityA](GetPhysicsContactEntityA), say which, where and how deep.

## Constraints

A constraint joins two bodies, or a body and the world when the second body is 0. [CreatePhysicsFixedConstraint](CreatePhysicsFixedConstraint) welds them, [CreatePhysicsPointConstraint](CreatePhysicsPointConstraint) lets them turn around a point, [CreatePhysicsHingeConstraint](CreatePhysicsHingeConstraint) around an axis, [CreatePhysicsSliderConstraint](CreatePhysicsSliderConstraint) lets one slide along an axis, [CreatePhysicsDistanceConstraint](CreatePhysicsDistanceConstraint) keeps them within a range of distances and [CreatePhysicsConeConstraint](CreatePhysicsConeConstraint) limits how far an axis may lean. Points and axes are in world space when the constraint is made. Both bodies must be in the same world.

[PhysicsConstraintLimits](PhysicsConstraintLimits), [PhysicsConstraintMotor](PhysicsConstraintMotor) and [PhysicsConstraintSpring](PhysicsConstraintSpring) change what a constraint allows, and angles are in degrees. [PhysicsConstraintBreakForce](PhysicsConstraintBreakForce) makes it give way under a load, which [GetPhysicsConstraintBroken](GetPhysicsConstraintBroken) reports. [FreePhysicsConstraint](FreePhysicsConstraint) removes one, and freeing either body does the same.
